concepts.name: I-JEPA
concepts.summary: Image Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (Assran et al., CVPR 2023): self-supervised learning by predicting the representations of masked image regions from visible context, in latent space rather than pixel space, so the model learns semantic gist instead of low-level texture.

concepts.name: Context encoder
concepts.summary: The trained branch of I-JEPA: an encoder that sees only the visible (unmasked) patches and is updated by gradient descent on the prediction loss — the Context Scribe whose quill is sharpened nightly by its errors.

concepts.name: EMA target encoder
concepts.summary: The gradient-free branch of I-JEPA: its weights are an exponential moving average of the context encoder (new target = 0.996 x old target + 0.004 x context). It encodes the full image to produce prediction targets, and because it cannot learn, it cannot collude in collapse.

concepts.name: Predictor network
concepts.summary: A narrow network between the two encoders: given the context encoder's representations of visible patches plus positional mask tokens marking where the occlusion lies, it conjures the target encoder's representation of the hidden region.

concepts.name: Masked latent prediction
concepts.summary: The I-JEPA objective: minimize the squared distance between predicted and true representations of masked regions — representation against representation, never pixel against pixel. Predicting in latent space returns the sense of what belongs, not the texture.

concepts.name: Representation collapse
concepts.summary: The failure mode of joint-embedding methods: all inputs mapped to one constant point, giving zero loss and zero information — the blank page with no regret. I-JEPA forbids it by learning asymmetry (EMA target, no gradient); VICReg forbids it with explicit variance and covariance penalties.

concepts.name: VICReg
concepts.summary: Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization (Bardes, Ponce and LeCun, ICLR 2022): a self-supervised loss of three explicit terms that prevents collapse without negative pairs or asymmetric networks, yielding representations that are semantically tight, globally spread, and dimensionally rich.

concepts.name: Invariance term
concepts.summary: VICReg's first vow: a mean-squared-error term pulling together the embeddings of two augmented views of the same image — two glimpses of the same thing must sound the same note.

concepts.name: Variance term
concepts.summary: VICReg's second vow, in open rebellion against the first: a hinge penalty keeps the standard deviation of each embedding dimension, computed across the batch, at no less than one — so the batch never collapses onto a single note.

concepts.name: Covariance term
concepts.summary: VICReg's third and subtlest vow: drive the off-diagonal entries of the embedding covariance matrix toward zero, decorrelating dimensions so the spread won by the variance term is not secretly crowded into a single direction (informational collapse).

concepts.name: Expander h-phi
concepts.summary: VICReg's projector: expands encoder output into a higher-dimensional space before the loss. It absorbs the invariance pressure so the encoder stays rich, and it turns nonlinear dependencies into linear correlations the covariance term can detect and remove. Discarded after training.

concepts.name: Projector head
concepts.summary: The funnel between encoder and self-supervised loss, discarded after training. It concentrates the pretext task's distortion within itself so the encoder beneath retains broadly useful features — a soft buffer, not a hard guard, since gradients still flow through it.

concepts.name: SimCLR
concepts.summary: Chen et al., ICML 2020: the simple contrastive framework whose authors first observed, almost by accident, that the encoder performs better downstream once the projection head is removed — the first sighting of the projector-head phenomenon, offered without a mathematics of the gradient.

concepts.name: Guillotine Regularization
concepts.summary: Bordes et al., NeurIPS 2023: snip off the head and the body sings on. Severing the projector after training can raise downstream performance by over thirty percentage points, because overfitting to the pretext task is localized in the head while the encoder is spared.

concepts.name: Gradient feature migration
concepts.summary: Xue et al., ICLR 2024: the implicit bias of gradient-based training makes pretext-useful features migrate toward the projector's output while downstream-useful features settle in the encoder. The head's non-linearities enable this emergent, non-architectural functional specialization.

concepts.name: Information bottleneck view
concepts.summary: ICLR 2025: the projection head is secretly an information bottleneck — it compresses out information irrelevant to the SSL objective and attenuates the gradient signal reaching the encoder, which sits upstream of the compression and so retains the broader signal.

concepts.name: The JEPA family
concepts.summary: The joint-embedding predictive architecture paradigm — predict in representation space, not pixel space — spanning I-JEPA, V-JEPA 2/2.1, and AMI Labs' world models. As of May 2026 it stands roughly at its GPT-3 moment: deployed, funded, and still awaiting its ChatGPT-equivalent.

concepts.name: V-JEPA 2 / 2.1
concepts.summary: Meta's video JEPA: pretrained on one million hours of video plus sixty-two hours of robot data, grasping novel objects at 65-80% on a Franka arm. V-JEPA 2.1 added Dense Predictive Loss, Deep Self-Supervision at intermediate layers, and modality-specific tokenizers: +20 points grasping, 10x faster planning; sizes from ViT-B (80M) to ViT-G (2B).

concepts.name: World Action Models
concepts.summary: The winter-2026 paradigm: one model jointly generates future video AND future action, instead of bolting perception onto action as VLAs do. DreamZero (NVIDIA, 14B, flow matching, 7 Hz), Fast-WAM (video prediction as a training-time representational enrichment, like BERT's masked tokens), MotuBrain (Mixture-of-Transformers, 95.8% on RoboTwin 2.0).

concepts.name: Marble / generative 3D worlds
concepts.summary: WorldLabs' Marble (Nov 2025): generates persistent, downloadable 3D worlds from text, image, video or sketch, represented as Gaussian Splatting — soft elliptical motes with color, opacity and orientation. Framed as the complement to JEPA: generative models create the worlds in which predictive agents train.

concepts.name: Scaling laws (the missing decree)
concepts.summary: Language models had the Chinchilla decree (Hoffmann et al., 2022: roughly 20 tokens per parameter), telling the field how to spend its compute. JEPA has no such decree yet — one of the four reasons the paradigm has not exploded commercially despite its technical merits.

concepts.name: Scaled dot-product attention
concepts.summary: The atomic operation of attention: Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) . V. Score every query against every key by dot product, scale by sqrt(d_k), soften to a probability distribution with softmax, then return the weighted blend of values. Score, scale, soften, blend.

concepts.name: Dot-product similarity
concepts.summary: Attention's measure of alignment: the dot product of a query and a key. For q=[1,0,2,1], the key [0,0,1,1] scores 3 while [1,1,0,0] scores 1, so the query leans toward the former. A larger dot product means greater likeness.

concepts.name: Softmax (normalise + sharpen)
concepts.summary: Softmax turns raw scores into attention weights, doing two jobs at once: it exponentiates (always positive, amplifying gaps so the winner wins by more) and normalises (weights sum to one). 'Normalise + sharpen': equal scores give near-uniform attention, large gaps give near one-hot. Preceded by scaling by sqrt(d_k) to keep gradients alive.

concepts.name: Q, K, V projections
concepts.summary: Q, K and V are three learned linear projections of the same input X (shape n x d_model): Q=X.Wq, K=X.Wk, V=X.Wv. The model learns what to ask, what to advertise, and what to give. Constraint: d_q = d_k always (the dot product demands it); d_v may differ.

concepts.name: The (n,n) score matrix — O(n²)
concepts.summary: The score matrix Q.K^T has shape (n, n) — every token's score to every token — making self-attention O(n^2) in sequence length. This (n,n) object is what later gets masked, cached, and (in Flash attention) never materialised.

concepts.name: Multi-head attention
concepts.summary: Run h attention operations in parallel, each in its own d_k = d_model/h subspace with its own Wq,Wk,Wv, then concatenate and mix with Wo: MultiHead = Concat(head_1..head_h).Wo. One head captures one notion of relevance; many heads capture many. d_model must be divisible by h.

concepts.name: Output projection Wo
concepts.summary: The (d_model x d_model) matrix Wo applied after concatenating heads. Concatenation alone keeps head subspaces isolated; Wo makes every output dimension a blend of all heads, weaving their separate insights into one representation.

concepts.name: Head specialisation and redundancy
concepts.summary: Heads specialise without any explicit diversity loss — difference emerges from random init, gradient pressure through Wo, and distinct subspaces. Yet trained heads end up partly redundant (20-40% are often prunable), which is exactly what motivates sharing keys and values in MQA and GQA.

concepts.name: Grouped-query attention (GQA)
concepts.summary: GQA shares one key/value pair across each GROUP of query heads: h query heads split into g groups. It interpolates between MHA (g=h, a KV pair per head) and MQA (g=1, one shared pair). LLaMA 2 70B uses g=8. An architecture choice made before training, shrinking the KV cache.

concepts.name: Multi-query attention (MQA)
concepts.summary: MQA keeps h independent query heads but a SINGLE shared Wk, Wv across all of them — eight researchers, one library — collapsing the KV cache up to 8-fold. It is the g=1 extreme of grouped-query attention, decided before training, not a post-hoc optimisation.

concepts.name: Causal masking
concepts.summary: In a decoder, a token must not attend to the future. Before softmax, the upper triangle of the (n,n) score matrix is set to -inf; since e^(-inf)=0, those positions get zero weight. This single change turns bidirectional attention into autoregressive generation. In code use a large negative number, and watch for NaNs from leaks.

concepts.name: Encoder vs decoder
concepts.summary: Names for which half of the 2017 Transformer a model keeps. Encoder = self-attention with NO mask (bidirectional, e.g. BERT). Decoder = self-attention with a causal mask (e.g. GPT, LLaMA). Decoder-only won the scaling race, but encoder-decoder lives on in T5, BART, and Whisper.

concepts.name: Self-attention
concepts.summary: Q, K and V all drawn from the same sequence — the tokens attend to one another. For 'The cat sat on the mat' the score matrix is (6,6); processing 'sat' should attend to its subject 'cat'. Different heads read the same sentence differently (syntactic, positional, determiner).

concepts.name: Cross-attention
concepts.summary: Attention where Q comes from one source and K, V from another — e.g. a text decoder querying image-encoder patches. The score matrix Q.K^T is (n_text, n_patches), not square. Output gives each text token visual information from the patches it attended to.

concepts.name: K and V come from where you look
concepts.summary: The unifying rule of attention: K and V always come from whatever you are looking INTO. Look into yourself -> self-attention; look into another modality -> cross-attention. The arithmetic is identical; only the source of keys and values changes.

concepts.name: Attention maps & head patterns
concepts.summary: The (n,n) softmax weight matrix IS the attention map; plotted as a heatmap (rows=queries, cols=keys, brightness=weight) it reveals learned head patterns: previous-token, first-token, subject-verb, induction, uniform (prunable), and diagonal self-attention heads.

concepts.name: ViT patch attention
concepts.summary: A Vision Transformer splits an image into patches (14x14 = 196) and attends over them, giving a (196,196) matrix. Take one query's 196 weights, reshape to 14x14, and overlay on the image; different heads attend to different regions (an object, an edge, the whole scene).

concepts.name: Modern VLMs skip cross-attention
concepts.summary: Most modern VLMs (SmolVLM, LLaVA, PaliGemma, Qwen-VL) skip explicit cross-attention: they project image patches into the LM's embedding space, concatenate them with text tokens, and let self-attention mix the modalities. Simpler and decoder-agnostic, but image tokens consume KV-cache and context budget.

concepts.name: KV cache
concepts.summary: At inference a decoder generates one token at a time; recomputing all past keys and values each step is wasteful. The KV cache stores every past token's K and V, so each new step computes only the new query, scores it against all cached keys, and blends the cached values. Grows by one entry per step per layer (per group in GQA).

concepts.name: Why Q is not cached
concepts.summary: Only K and V are cached, never Q. The query is the asker: it asks once and moves on, so caching it would only ever reuse its last row. Keys and values are the label and content that every future query must still consult. Unlike an RNN, each new query has direct access to all past K,V — nothing is compressed.

concepts.name: The Transformer block
concepts.summary: The repeating unit: LayerNorm -> Multi-Head Attention -> +residual -> LayerNorm -> MLP -> +residual. Attention is inter-token mixing ('who to listen to', like spatial conv); the MLP is per-token processing ('what to do with it', like 1x1 conv). Residuals are the gradient highway; input shape equals output shape, so blocks stack (L=32 for 7B, L=96 for GPT-4 class).

concepts.name: Flash attention
concepts.summary: An exact (not approximate) attention that never materialises the (n,n) score matrix in slow HBM. It tiles Q and K into fast on-chip SRAM and keeps a running softmax (running max m, running sum l, correcting by e^(m_old-m_new)), cutting memory from O(n^2) to O(n) while producing identical output.

concepts.name: Embedding & lm_head
concepts.summary: The two learned layers bracketing a Transformer: the token embedding (vocab_size x d_model lookup, a sparse gather of the used rows) and the lm_head / W_vocab (d_model -> vocab logits, a full matmul). Often tied (W_vocab = embedding^T). Rare tokens, looked up seldom, receive fewer gradient updates.

concepts.name: Positional encoding
concepts.summary: Bare attention is permutation-equivariant — it sees content, not order — so position must be injected. Two fixed, precomputed families do it: sinusoidal encodings ADD a position signal to embeddings, while RoPE ROTATES queries and keys; both use frequencies freq_i = 1/10000^(2i/d).

concepts.name: Sinusoidal positional encoding
concepts.summary: Fixed sin/cos position vectors added to token embeddings before the Q,K,V projections. Each dimension pair gets its own frequency freq_i = 1/10000^(2i/d) — fast hands and slow hands, like a clock — so every position has a unique code. Encodes ABSOLUTE position; a learned-table variant cannot extrapolate past its training length.

concepts.name: RoPE (rotary position embedding)
concepts.summary: Rotary Position Embedding rotates Q and K (not V) by an angle m.theta proportional to position, after projection. Because a dot product of vectors rotated by m.theta and n.theta depends only on (m-n).theta (via cos(A-B)), RoPE encodes RELATIVE distance and preserves length. Favoured by modern long-context models.
